Shannon's sampling theory, in the form of generalized sampling and its variants, is the most effective solution to the reconstruction problem for the class of signals and sampling scenarios considered in this paper.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for nonideal sampling, a shift-invariant regularization is optimal, and the generating function is determined by the regularization operator.
, when the sampling is nonideal, the best reconstruction space for a given regularization is not necessarily bandlimited.
the continuous-space solution of the generalized sampling and regularization problem belongs to a shift invariant space, which can be characterized by a generating function.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for a wide range of realistic settings, the best reconstruction space is not necessarily the space of bandlimited functions, and the reconstruction of a bandlimited function is not necessarily the best solution.

, in the absence of a priori knowledge, the best reconstruction space is the one generated by the generalized B-spline corresponding to the regularization operator that minimizes the mean squared error (MSE) of the continuous-space solution.
the shift-invariant space of the continuous-domain reconstruction is the natural choice for the regularization space in the sampling problem.
